title: The Missing Handoff
hypothesis: A recipient-approved, volunteer-optional, explicitly checked offer-to-shelf handoff could address an existing sourcing or food rescue logistics friction. No current recipient or donor has confirmed this is their unmet step.
firstContact: Waseca Area Neighborhood Service Center, director@wasecaservicecenter.org — inquiry only; not a partner
secondContact: Waseca Area Food Cooperative and MSU supply-chain instructor — inquiry only; current contact not yet verified

facts.title: Supply squeeze at Waseca Food Shelf
facts.body: WANSC reports rising need, reduced access to discounted food-bank stock, and more costly wholesale/retail sourcing. Historical data must not be represented as live inventory.

facts.title: Surplus produce and possible harvest help
facts.body: The food shelf director welcomed fresh garden produce and said volunteers might help harvest. The report records June 2026 service to 680 households and more than 20,000 pounds of food.

facts.title: Waseca co-op + university already studying logistics
facts.body: The Waseca Area Food Cooperative's MSU supply-chain course discussion included local produce sourcing, voucher processes and food rescue logistics. Their work must not be duplicated or claimed as ours.

facts.title: SROC has a documented harvest-sharing precedent
facts.body: UMN reported more than two tons of produce donated from SROC research during the 2025 growing season. This does not establish any available crop in late 2026.

facts.title: UMN has practical farm-to-grocery methods
facts.body: Extension provides regulatory, labeling, safe-handling, invoice and distribution guidance to reuse rather than reinvent.

doors.name: Waseca Area Neighborhood Service Center
doors.ask: Ask whether any particular source-to-shelf handoff needs attention; the receiving shelf names its own problem.

doors.name: Waseca Area Food Cooperative / MSU
doors.ask: Ask whether their existing food rescue logistics coursework could use a small software method rather than duplicate it.
doors.gate: Co-op and course owners have not opted in.

doors.name: University of Minnesota Extension
doors.ask: Ask for method review on food safety, farm-to-grocery fit and what no new system should replace.

doors.name: MIT Solve 2027 Climate
doors.ask: Explore a prototype addressing resilient and equitable local food distribution, only with credible stage and outcome evidence.
doors.gate: Deadline November 6, 2026 noon EST; a synthetic-only demo may not qualify.

doors.name: Code for America Demo Lab
doors.ask: Show a 60-second demonstration of accountable, receiver-governed sourcing.

doors.name: Rochester Hunger Task Force
doors.ask: Ask if a separate Rochester-defined last-mile problem merits a local comparison.
doors.gate: Rochester has not defined or authorized our pilot.

doors.name: Rockefeller / Cities Deliver
doors.ask: Later explore an eligible lead + qualifying municipality for accountable food-service AI.
doors.gate: A city letter and eligible organizational applicant are absent.

doors.name: BLOOM Civic Host
doors.ask: Let local people deliberate over what AI may and may not decide in food distribution.
doors.gate: Must be locally convened, human-led, with the host's permission.

doors.name: Institute of Global Homelessness
doors.ask: Seek feedback on a transferrable no-case-data essential-goods method.
doors.gate: No recipient, shelter or country has opted in.

doors.name: Digital Public Goods Alliance
doors.ask: Assess a separable open source handoff contract against published standards.
